newsitem.title: USA: Tosco, union reach tentative refinery pact.
newsitem.headline: Tosco, union reach tentative refinery pact.

text.p: Tosco Corp and the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers Union (OCAW) said they reached a tentative agreement on Monday on a new labour contract for four California refineries.
Tosco is buying the four refineries from Unocal Corp and assumes ownership on March 31. Tosco's contract negotiations with the union had stalled last week.

The OCAW still has outstanding issues with Unocal relating to the sale of the refineries and had threatened to strike if they were not resolved. An OCAW official said a strike remained an option but he did not expect it to happen on Monday night.
The OCAW represents 900 workers, roughly half the workforce, at the four refineries.

Tosco officials and OCAW negotiators met in southern California on Monday and reached a tentative agreement on the new labour contract for when Tosco takes over the refineries, company and union officials said.
"This afternoon, they (company negotiators) did reach a tentative agreement with the OCAW on all issues," Tosco spokeswoman Linda Saltzman said.
The tentative agreement was subject to ratification by the union's members, Saltzman said, adding that the vote was expected before next Monday.
"All parties are very pleased and very hopeful that this series of negotiations will be completed and successful," she added. She gave no details of the proposed new contract.
Bill McGoveran, western region director for the OCAW, confirmed a tentative agreement had been reached but declined to give details pending a vote by union members.
He expected union members to vote on the tentative agreement this week and over the weekend.
McGoveran said there were still "very serious issues" to be resolved with Unocal related to the sale of the refineries, including severance pay and pensions.
In a letter to Unocal last week, the OCAW threatened to terminate its contract late on Monday, giving workers the option to strike.
The union's decision would depend on Unocal's response now that the OCAW had reached an agreement with Tosco, McGoveran said. If Unocal refused to negotiate, a strike was still an option, he said.
He said he anticipated that "a strike would not happen tonight but by tomorrow things are going to be moving in a (decisive) direction."
